precepts.text: Yet I loved Jacob, just like he loved Abel, and I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste: allowed him to be overthrown. Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished: we lost all, we're going back to being vagabonds. But we will return and build the desolate places: build up ourselves as an empire, like Cain built that city. They shall build, but I will throw down. And they shall call them the border of wickedness: the beginning and the end of wickedness. And the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever: no repentance, no salvation, no kingdom, ever. Not even the good ones, so some of you coons out there.
precepts.point: The Bible calls the evil man, or the violent man, the wicked. Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man, who have purposed to overthrow my goings.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
The evil man and the violent man of Psalms 140 has a name, and Malachi gives it. “I have loved you, saith the Lord.” Israel asks, “Wherein hast thou loved us?” And the answer: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” He loved Jacob just like he loved Abel, and he hated Esau. Laying his mountains and his heritage waste means God allowed him to be overthrown.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: we lost all, we are going back to being vagabonds. “but we will return and build the desolate places”: build themselves back up as an empire, just like Cain built that city. And the Lord answers, “They shall build, but I will throw down.”

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: the beginning and the end of wickedness. “and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: no repentance, no salvation, no kingdom, ever. Not even the good ones, so some of you coons out there.

So when David prays “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man” and “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”, this is who he is praying against: Esau, Edom, the people the Lord hated and against whom he hath indignation for ever.

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven, that's Israel, suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The violent is the Romans; Esau is the Romans. Esau is the violent man, the wicked man.
precepts.point: The Bible calls the evil man, or the violent man, the wicked. Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man, who have purposed to overthrow my goings.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven, that's Israel, and Israel suffereth violence. The violent that take it by force are the Romans, and Esau is the Romans.

That puts a name on the man of Psalms 140. The Bible calls the evil man, the violent man, the wicked, and Esau is the violent man, the wicked man. “They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips”: they are liars. And they “have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

So David's cry, “preserve me from the violent man”, is Israel's cry to be kept from the hands of Esau, the Romans, who have done violence to the kingdom of heaven from the days of John the Baptist until now.

precepts.text: Deliver me from the evil man, preserve me from the violent man, which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war, from Venezuela to Iran to Mexico and Cuba. They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent, mocking Spain for refusing them; adders' poison, their philosophies and politics, is under their lips. Keep me from the hands of the wicked, who have purposed to overthrow my goings; the proud have hid a snare and spread a net and set gins for me. Selah.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Psalms 140 proves who the people are that delight in war. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man.” Psalms 68 said scatter the nations that delight in war; don't you see Trump and them delighting in war?

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” You thought it would end with Venezuela. Oh, no. He said we are going to hit Iran. You thought it ended there; next week Mexico, and maybe Cuba. The party is not over.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent”: the things they say. Don't you hear them mocking the nations? They wanted to land in Spain, Spain said no, and now they are mad and talking about Spain. And “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their philosophies, their religions, their politics. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”: this so-called white man, keep me from their hands. Then, “preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” They purposed to overthrow the goings of the children of Israel. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.” Traps all around.

These are the fierce nations of Isaiah 33:19. When the Lord scatters them, we shall not see that fierce people any more, and Jerusalem will be a quiet habitation.

precepts.text: Deliver me from the evil man, preserve me from the violent man, which imagine mischiefs and are continually gathered together for war. If there is no war he will start one; it is his nature. Their tongues are sharpened like a serpent with adder's poison, and they hide snares, cords, nets and gins.
precepts.point: When the Lord awakes and intervenes, he shall despise their image. That image is Cesare Borgia, the fake Jesus who represents all Edom.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.” They have so much wealth that pride covers them like a chain, and much of their old slave money is invested in war companies, weaponry and the military. David names him: “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man”. This is about the white man. Preserve us from him.

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” If there is no war, you can bet your last dollar the white man will start one. He can never let there be peace on earth; the way God made him, it is his nature. Trump pledged to end global conflict and bombed at least seven countries in 2025; under Obama in 2016, 26,171 bombs were dropped on seven countries. And they took Maduro with weapons that shut his military down in minutes.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips. Selah.” Selah means it is true. Whatever comes out of their mouth, religion or politics, is the worst kind of poison; for some of them politics is their religion. Take hold of it and you will die.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” Their purpose on earth is to overthrow the twelve tribes of Israel. They can't rest if they see one of us in a nice car or a nice home: he must be selling drugs. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me.” The cords and the net are their traps of religion and politics, and a gin is a trap too. He is the wicked of Job 9:24 and Malachi 1, and he wears violence like he wears clothes.

precepts.text: Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man, who have purposed to overthrow my goings. The spiritual Satan and the physical Satan work as a team, in your head asleep or awake and jumping into people at your job.
precepts.point: Get rid of your own personal demonic sin before you line a brother up for his failure. In the furnace every evil thought and secret act against the congregation comes back.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
Christ said “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, and “be thou faithful unto death”. David shows who is working against us: “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

The purpose of the wicked is to overthrow your goings. You think Satan is sleeping? There is the spiritual Satan and the physical Satan, and every time they are at work, they are working as a team. He will get in your head while you sleep or get in your head while you are awake. At your job, Satan comes jumping into people, and you see people react some type of way.

This is war. That is why you must prepare your soul for the pain that is coming with their children, Esau's children. Whatever state you find yourself in, jail, about to be put to death, afflicted, tortured, losing an eye or an arm, be faithful, because pain is part of the walk. The body is not you; your soul is you.

Mark 9 shows how that spirit works in us: “ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”. That is us destroying ourselves in the club, the partying and religion, because Satan is in us and we thought it was the way. So pray to be kept from the hands of the wicked, and ask the Lord to strengthen your faith, because when your faith is weak, Satan keeps attacking you.

precepts.text: Evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.
precepts.point: The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, saying, who shall bring me down to the ground? Trump now talks exactly like that.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” There is a set time for the times of the Gentiles to be fulfilled, with Esau at the top, that same spirit of Cain in rulership. But it is temporary. Waiting generation after generation for his judgment, the pride of his heart has deceived him. He forgot what his judgment is and thinks he is untouchable, especially after seeing what his weapons did to the air defences of Russia and China.

Now Trump is talking like that. On Air Force One after capturing Maduro he names the countries he will come after: Colombia, run by a sick man; Mexico, where the cartels are running things. He says the vice president of Venezuela will face a situation probably worse than Maduro, and emphasises how fast and violent it was: it was very violent. That office once had prestige, and though they did their evil, they at least spoke well. He is not even bothering with appearances anymore.

David shows where that ends: “Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth: evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” You reap what you sow. What he puts out is the exact same way his demise is going to come.

That is the lineage of Cain: Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and where others saw tools his mind saw weapons. Murder led to industry, hatred to technology, and violence to institutional power. Esau was told, “by thy sword shalt thou live.” But who shall bring him down to the ground? It is prophesied: first all those he dealt with will turn against him, and then Christ and his elect will have the glory and the honour to take him down.

note.label: Genesis 32: Wrestling Until the Blessing

precepts.why:
“Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.”

That is what Jacob understood was coming toward him: Esau with four hundred men, the violent man that imagines mischiefs in his heart and is continually gathered together for war. Esau had purposed in his heart to slay him, and now he came with an army. Jacob's prayer for deliverance fit the psalm.

note.label: Psalm 140: Deliver Me From the Evil Man

precepts.why: “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man”. David is not talking about everyone who commits wickedness but a particular person, and the key points show who: one “Which imagine mischiefs in their heart”. “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.” The evil man is the one who devises iniquity and works evil upon his bed, and this points to Esau.

precepts.text: His words were smoother than butter but war was in his heart; his words softer than oil yet drawn swords, confirming this is the evil man, Esau, the nation of Edom.
precepts.point: The key points show us who he is talking about: one who imagines mischief in his heart, who is continually gathered together for war, whose tongue is sharpened like a serpent with adder's poison under his lips.
